name: IL-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 6 points on the partisan baseline
Bill Foster is a well-funded incumbent with $2.5M on hand
Republican challenger raised only $311K with $23K cash remaining
model.rationale: Foster holds a strong structural advantage: a D+6 district, incumbency, and a massive cash edge over a challenger who has almost nothing banked. Markets price this at 96% Democratic, consistent with fundamentals pointing to a roughly 19-point margin.
model.watch: Any late outside spending against Foster or a polling surprise showing the challenger within single digits would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bill Foster seeks another term in a suburban Chicago district that leans Democratic by six points. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, holding $2.5 million on hand after raising $2.2 million, while Republican Jeff Walter has raised about $311 thousand and reports only $23 thousand in the bank. No outside groups are spending in the race.

With no public polling available, the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, the favorable national environment for Democrats, incumbency, and the money gap. Prediction markets give Foster roughly a 96% chance of winning, and the seat is rated Safe Democratic.
